sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做DJ时，你每晚也要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后把DJ台变成一个活生生的、快闪式的博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、已有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the rise of the far-right in Europe.
sentences.zh: 今天的话题：欧洲极右翼势力的崛起。

sentences.en: Months after Donald Trump's populist victory in the United States,
sentences.zh: 在唐纳德·特朗普在美国取得民粹主义胜利几个月后，

sentences.en: Europe's political reckoning begins as voters there confront similar questions of immigration and national identity.
sentences.zh: 随着欧洲选民面临移民和民族认同等类似问题，欧洲的政治清算开始了。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, March 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月14日，星期二。

sentences.en: Western governments remain dangerously blind to the danger of Islamization.
sentences.zh: 西方政府对伊斯兰化的危险依然危险地视而不见。

sentences.en: Islam is a religion of peace, they say, but that is a lie.
sentences.zh: 他们说伊斯兰教是和平的宗教，但那是谎言。

sentences.en: The Netherlands is known for its liberal politics and socialist government.
sentences.zh: 荷兰以其自由主义政治和社会主义政府而闻名。

sentences.en: Look at what happened at Istanbul Airport.
sentences.zh: 看看伊斯坦布尔机场发生了什么。

sentences.en: Look at what happened in Orlando a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 看看几周前奥兰多发生了什么。

sentences.en: But in this week's elections there, a far-right candidate for prime minister, Gert Wilders, is surging in popularity.
sentences.zh: 但在本周的选举中，极右翼总理候选人吉尔特·威尔德斯的支持率正在飙升。

sentences.en: Look at what happened in San Bernardino last December.
sentences.zh: 看看去年12月圣贝纳迪诺发生了什么。

sentences.en: The list is endless.
sentences.zh: 这样的例子不胜枚举。

sentences.en: And everything this list has in common is Islam.
sentences.zh: 而这份名单上所有事件的共同点就是伊斯兰教。

sentences.en: Donald Trump isn't the only politician striking nativist themes and gaining a popular following.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普并不是唯一一个打着本土主义旗号并获得大众追随的政治家。

sentences.en: It's happening in continental Europe, too.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在欧洲大陆也在发生。

sentences.en: I think Marine Le Pen is going to win.
sentences.zh: 我认为玛丽娜·勒庞会赢。

sentences.en: I think she'll be the next president of France.
sentences.zh: 我认为她会成为下一任法国总统。

sentences.en: No way.
sentences.zh: 不可能。

sentences.en: I, way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很有可能。

sentences.en: Austria and the Freedom Party took 36 percent of the vote in presidential elections over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 奥地利自由党在上周末的总统选举中获得了36%的选票。

sentences.en: The far-right is on the rise.
sentences.zh: 极右翼正在崛起。

sentences.en: How did we get to this moment?
sentences.zh: 我们是如何走到这一步的？

sentences.en: There's a perception and a reality.
sentences.zh: 这既有认知上的，也有现实层面的原因。

sentences.en: Thank you guys for coming on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们二位能来。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Max Fischer and Amanda Taub are the interpreters.
sentences.zh: 马克斯·费舍尔和阿曼达·陶布是我们的解读嘉宾。

sentences.en: So you guys have been spending the past year traveling all around Europe watching the rise of what is called the far-right in country after country.
sentences.zh: 你们过去一年一直在欧洲各地旅行，观察着所谓极右翼在各个国家的崛起。

sentences.en: What's the perception of why this movement is becoming so ascendant?
sentences.zh: 对于为什么这种运动变得如此盛行，人们是怎么看的？

sentences.en: So I think the popular narrative that's forming is that this is an issue of kind of economic inequality,
sentences.zh: 我认为目前形成的主流叙事是，这是一种经济不平等的问题，

sentences.en: that this is something that's happening in kind of sad, depressed, former industrial towns where the factories have closed or maybe places that have been hit by globalization.
sentences.zh: 认为这发生在那些工厂倒闭、悲伤萧条的前工业城镇，或者是受全球化冲击的地方。

sentences.en: And they're kind of lashing out at their lack of economic opportunities and they're frightened of economic competition from immigrants.
sentences.zh: 他们是在发泄对缺乏经济机会的不满，并且害怕来自移民的经济竞争。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing is that the data just doesn't really support it.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，数据并不支持这种说法。

sentences.en: So like who it actually is, is it's white, it's blue collar, it's people who might not necessarily have a college education,
sentences.zh: 实际上，支持者多为白人、蓝领，可能没有受过大学教育，

sentences.en: but actually tend to be doing okay economically and are like a little bit on the richer end for their cohort.
sentences.zh: 但他们的经济状况往往还不错，在同龄人中甚至属于较富裕的一端。

sentences.en: These are people for whom the economy is working.
sentences.zh: 这些人其实是全球化经济的受益者。

sentences.en: And we've kind of centered on this like, oh, losers of globalization narrative.
sentences.zh: 我们一直聚焦于“全球化输家”这种叙事。

sentences.en: They are losing out, but it's in a subtler way that is so sensitive.
sentences.zh: 他们确实在失去什么，但那是一种非常微妙且敏感的失去。

sentences.en: We don't even like to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至都不愿谈论它。

sentences.en: Let's talk about it.
sentences.zh: 那我们就来谈谈吧。

sentences.en: What's the real explanation for the rise of the far right in Europe?
sentences.zh: 欧洲极右翼崛起的真正解释是什么？

sentences.en: So I think what this is really about is immigration and demographics.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真正关乎的是移民和人口结构问题。

sentences.en: A lot of these countries used to be much whiter.
sentences.zh: 很多这些国家过去白人比例要高得多。

sentences.en: They used to be more separate before the European Union.
sentences.zh: 在欧盟成立之前，它们彼此之间更加独立。

sentences.en: And then in the last few years, there's been a really sudden influx of people.
sentences.zh: 而在过去几年里，人口突然大量涌入。

sentences.en: And I think it's provoked a lot of stress.
sentences.zh: 我认为这引发了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: And that is what is driving a lot of this politics.
sentences.zh: 这正是驱动这些政治现象的原因。

sentences.en: They are losing out in the sense that about 50 years ago, we in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们所说的“失去”，是指大约50年前，我们美国

sentences.en: and Europe had this big debate over, on the one hand, we're liberal democracies that want to be pluralistic and we're very diverse.
sentences.zh: 和欧洲进行了一场大辩论：一方面，我们是想要多元化、包容性强的自由民主国家；

sentences.en: But on the other hand, for a very long time, we've had national identities that are built around a specific demographic group, white and Christian.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，长期以来，我们的民族认同是建立在特定的群体——白人和基督徒——之上的。

sentences.en: And like those two things are in tension.
sentences.zh: 这两者之间存在着张力。

sentences.en: What are we going to do about it?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: The way that debate resolved 50 years ago was with this idea called Cosapolitanism, which is let's have a new identity that includes everybody and we're all equal.
sentences.zh: 50年前解决这场辩论的方式是提出“世界主义”理念，即建立一种包含所有人、人人平等的共同身份。

sentences.en: But that means that the majority groups in Western societies, whites,
sentences.zh: 但这意味着西方社会的主体群体——白人，

sentences.en: are going from a place of privilege in society and having society kind of molded to look like them and serve them first to that not being the case.
sentences.zh: 将从社会特权地位，即社会按照他们的样子塑造并优先服务于他们，转变为不再享有这种特权。

sentences.en: That is a form of losing out and people are pushing back against that.
sentences.zh: 这是一种“失去”，人们正在对此进行反击。

sentences.en: And that has been accelerated in recent years by this big wave of migration in Europe, by some economic changes.
sentences.zh: 近年来，欧洲的大规模移民潮和一些经济变化加速了这一进程。

sentences.en: But these are not people who are losing their jobs to China.
sentences.zh: 但这些人并不是因为中国而丢了工作的人。

sentences.en: These are people who are losing their privileged place in society.
sentences.zh: 这些人失去的是他们在社会中的特权地位。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, before we get too far, what is the far right in Europe and how is it different from the right in the United States?
sentences.zh: 在深入探讨之前，什么是欧洲的极右翼？它与美国的右翼有何不同？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So I think the best way to think about the far right is not as really left or right in the way we think about it in U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为看待极右翼最好的方式，不是用我们美国政治中那种左右派的思维，

sentences.en: politics, but as basically a form of us versus them identity politics.
sentences.zh: 而是将其视为一种“我们与他们”的身份政治。

sentences.en: So it's all about defining a group that is us and should get, you know, the benefits of citizenship and the benefits of, you know,
sentences.zh: 它完全在于界定一个“我们”的群体，他们应该获得公民身份的好处，获得

sentences.en: the welfare state and rights and things like that versus a group that is them right now.
sentences.zh: 福利国家、权利等方面的利益，而与之相对的是“他们”这个群体。

sentences.en: Now, in the case of the European far right, that group is immigrants and particularly Muslim immigrants who they are pointing to as them who are dangerous.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲极右翼的语境下，这个群体就是移民，特别是被他们指为危险的穆斯林移民。

sentences.en: And right now we're in a period of change.
sentences.zh: 现在我们正处于一个变革时期。

sentences.en: So the last few years, there have been really rapid changes because of the refugee crisis.
sentences.zh: 过去几年，由于难民危机，变化非常迅速。

sentences.en: Let me just slow this down for a minute.
sentences.zh: 让我把节奏放慢一点。

sentences.en: When we talk about refugee crisis and Europe, just how big a change is this for any one country in Europe?
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论欧洲难民危机时，这对欧洲任何一个国家来说，变化到底有多大？

sentences.en: Starting in about 2014, they keep coming thousands every day at the main train station.
sentences.zh: 从2014年左右开始，每天都有成千上万的人涌入主火车站。

sentences.en: There are so many of them, all of them.
sentences.zh: 他们人数众多，全都是人。

sentences.en: They just want to go inside.
sentences.zh: 他们只想进去。

sentences.en: Large numbers of refugees started coming across the Mediterranean into Europe.
sentences.zh: 大量难民开始跨越地中海进入欧洲。

sentences.en: Desperate men and women who'd handed over hundreds of dollars to cross the Mediterranean in small, overcrowded boats.
sentences.zh: 绝望的男男女女交了数百美元，挤在狭小拥挤的船上横渡地中海。

sentences.en: The result has been that millions of people have come to Europe to seek asylum and refugee status.
sentences.zh: 结果就是数以百万计的人来到欧洲寻求庇护和难民身份。

sentences.en: Often greeted by applauding locals or welcoming volunteers.
sentences.zh: 他们常常受到当地人鼓掌欢迎或志愿者的接待。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing is that the political response has pretty much been very similar across Europe.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，整个欧洲的政治反应却出奇地一致。

sentences.en: Not everyone welcomes the newcomers.
sentences.zh: 并非所有人都欢迎这些新来者。

sentences.en: Early Monday morning, a fire burned down a shelter for 80 refugees.
sentences.zh: 周一清晨，一场大火烧毁了一个容纳80名难民的收容所。

sentences.en: Five retreated at hospital.
sentences.zh: 五人被送往医院。

sentences.en: Which is the rise of this kind of populist politics where people say they're afraid of immigrants, they're afraid of this kind of change and they want to restore control.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种民粹主义政治的崛起，人们说他们害怕移民，害怕这种变化，想要恢复控制权。

sentences.en: Well, so when I think about this kind of us versus them and wonder where this is coming from, my mind always goes back to this fascinating 2002 Harvard study of Somalia.
sentences.zh: 那么，当我思考这种“我们与他们”的对立，并想知道它从何而来时，我的脑海里总是浮现出哈佛大学2002年关于索马里的那项迷人研究。

sentences.en: So stay with me.
sentences.zh: 听我说下去。

sentences.en: This is going to make sense.
sentences.zh: 这会讲得通的。

sentences.en: It used to be the case back in, I think, the 80s.
sentences.zh: 我想在80年代的时候，情况还是这样的。

sentences.en: If you ask people in Somalia, like, hey, what is your ethnicity?
sentences.zh: 如果你问索马里人：“嘿，你的种族是什么？

sentences.en: What is your identity?
sentences.zh: 你的身份是什么？”

sentences.en: They would say Somali.
sentences.zh: 他们会说：索马里人。

sentences.en: They would say that's who I am.
sentences.zh: 他们会说这就是我是谁。

sentences.en: Just like if you would ask, you know, most Americans, what's your identity?
sentences.zh: 就像如果你问大多数美国人：“你的身份是什么？”

sentences.en: They would say American.
sentences.zh: 他们会说：美国人。

sentences.en: But then something really interesting started to happen when they had a big food shortage and famine in the 90s is that this period of scarcity and resource competition where people couldn't get enough.
sentences.zh: 但在90年代发生严重粮食短缺和饥荒时，一件非常有趣的事情发生了，那就是在资源匮乏和竞争的时期，人们无法获得足够的物资。

sentences.en: Researchers started going back and asking people again their identity and they didn't say Somali anymore.
sentences.zh: 研究人员开始回去再次询问人们的身份，他们不再说自己是索马里人了。

sentences.en: They started to reference their clan.
sentences.zh: 他们开始提到自己的氏族。

sentences.en: And then over time, they started to go for even more granular senses of identity like a sub clan or tribal group.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们开始追求更细化的身份认同，比如次氏族或部落群体。

sentences.en: And so what you saw happening is that people literally changed how they thought of their own identity.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的是，人们确实改变了他们对自己身份的看法。

sentences.en: In Europe and Western societies, it's a subtler form of scarcity and resource competition.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲和西方社会，这是一种更微妙的稀缺和资源竞争。

sentences.en: It is the perception it's not real, but the perception that jobs are becoming harder to get.
sentences.zh: 这是一种认知，虽然不是现实，但人们认为工作变得越来越难找了。

sentences.en: And so, like, therefore, migrants must be competing with me for those jobs.
sentences.zh: 因此，移民一定是在和我竞争这些工作。

sentences.en: And how does that play into the phenomenon of the rise of the far right?
sentences.zh: 这又是如何影响极右翼崛起这一现象的呢？

sentences.en: Because the far right is willing to say what no other mainstream party is willing to say, which is, yeah, you are in competition with these other groups.
sentences.zh: 因为极右翼愿意说出其他主流政党不敢说的话，那就是：没错，你确实在与其他群体竞争。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Immigrants are scary.
sentences.zh: 移民很可怕。

sentences.en: They are coming to take your jobs.
sentences.zh: 他们来抢你的工作。

sentences.en: They are a threat to your identity.
sentences.zh: 他们是对你身份的威胁。

sentences.en: You are different from them.
sentences.zh: 你和他们不同。

sentences.en: They're not part of us.
sentences.zh: 他们不是我们的一员。

sentences.en: You can't see me, but I'm air quoting us.
sentences.zh: 你看不见我，但我正在用空气引号强调“我们”。

sentences.en: None of that, strictly speaking, is true.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，这些都不是真的。

sentences.en: In fact, immigrant assimilation has gone fine for a very long time in Europe.
sentences.zh: 事实上，移民融入在欧洲已经顺利进行了很长一段时间。

sentences.en: But these far right groups that are outside of the political mainstream are willing to say things that nobody else is willing to say.
sentences.zh: 但这些游离于政治主流之外的极右翼团体，愿意说出没人敢说的话。

sentences.en: And that really appeals to this sense that people have of a, like, fracturing, narrower identity in conflict with other groups.
sentences.zh: 这确实迎合了人们心中那种身份破碎、狭隘，并与其他群体发生冲突的感觉。

sentences.en: And if the European populations, as you two have both said, are essentially wrong about just how much a threat these new people coming into their countries are,
sentences.zh: 如果正如你们两位所说，欧洲民众对于这些新来者构成的威胁程度本质上是错误的，

sentences.en: then what exactly is triggering this sense of scarcity to go back to Somalia?
sentences.zh: 那么到底是什么触发了这种稀缺感，回到索马里的例子？

sentences.en: Even if it's sort of an illusion, is it potentially terrorism?
sentences.zh: 即使这是一种错觉，它有可能是恐怖主义吗？

sentences.en: I think terrorism is a way to talk about this, but it's not really what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我认为恐怖主义是谈论这个问题的一种方式，但这并不是真正发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, I just went to this town called Pankow.
sentences.zh: 我刚去了潘科这个城镇。

sentences.en: It's a neighborhood, actually, of Berlin on the outskirts of the city.
sentences.zh: 其实它是柏林郊区的一个街区。

sentences.en: And the AFD has done really well there.
sentences.zh: 德国选择党（AFD）在那里表现得非常好。

sentences.en: A far-right anti-immigrant party in Germany has made big gains in three regional elections.
sentences.zh: 这个德国极右翼反移民政党在三次地区选举中取得了巨大进展。

sentences.en: That have only been around for a few years.
sentences.zh: 他们成立才不过几年。

sentences.en: The Alternative for Germany, or AFD, has secured enough votes to enter state parliaments.
sentences.zh: 德国选择党（AFD）已经获得了足够的选票进入州议会。

sentences.en: In this district, they won more votes than any other party.
sentences.zh: 在这个选区，他们赢得的选票比任何其他政党都多。

sentences.en: They've done extremely well in local elections.
sentences.zh: 他们在地方选举中表现极其出色。

sentences.en: And in national elections, they're polling at about 15 percent right now, which in Germany is a lot.
sentences.zh: 在全国选举中，他们目前的民调支持率约为15%，在德国这已经很高了。

sentences.en: So, there's something going on there.
sentences.zh: 所以，那里确实发生了一些事情。

sentences.en: They see what's going on in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了柏林正在发生什么。

sentences.en: Thousands come out to proteSt.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人出来抗议。

sentences.en: Their message, no more refugees.
sentences.zh: 他们的口号是：不要再有难民了。

sentences.en: Germany is full.
sentences.zh: 德国已经满了。

sentences.en: Which has taken a lot of refugees and also just seen a lot of immigration in recent years.
sentences.zh: 德国近年来接收了大量难民，也看到了大量移民涌入。

sentences.en: And to some people, that seems interesting and cool.
sentences.zh: 对一些人来说，这看起来很有趣且很酷。

sentences.en: But to some people, it seems frightening.
sentences.zh: 但对另一些人来说，这看起来很可怕。

sentences.en: Every Monday night, he told us, we come together peacefully.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我们，每个周一晚上，我们都会和平地聚集在一起。

sentences.en: We are not Nazis, he says.
sentences.zh: 我们不是纳粹，他说。

sentences.en: We don't want to be labeled as Nazis.
sentences.zh: 我们不想被贴上纳粹的标签。

sentences.en: And we don't want to be painted into the right-wing corner.
sentences.zh: 我们也不想被归入右翼阵营。

sentences.en: We just don't want to become strangers in our own country, he says.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不想在自己的国家变成陌生人，他说。

sentences.en: The issue is that the places where you see this big far-right backlash are not places that themselves experience a lot of immigration.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，你看到极右翼强烈反弹的地方，并不是那些本身经历大量移民的地方。

sentences.en: But they are next to...
sentences.zh: 但它们毗邻……

sentences.en: Dear citizens of Berlin...
sentences.zh: 亲爱的柏林市民们……

sentences.en: ...towns getting lots of immigration.
sentences.zh: ……那些接收了大量移民的城镇。

sentences.en: This idea of a free society that shows solidarity,
sentences.zh: 这种自由社会展现团结的理念，

sentences.en: this is what many people from all over the world think of when they think of our tolerant and open-minded city or Berlin city that is open to the world.
sentences.zh: 正是世界各地许多人在想到我们这座宽容、开明，或者说拥抱世界的柏林城时，脑海中浮现的景象。

sentences.en: And it's that proximity that is leading people to have this backlash.
sentences.zh: 正是这种亲密接触导致了人们的抵触情绪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Social scientists call this the halo effect because often it means that there's this ring around big cities that almost looks like a halo of pretty white working-class suburbs that support far-right parties.
sentences.zh: 社会学家称之为“光环效应”，因为这通常意味着大城市周围环绕着一圈光环，看起来就像是一圈支持极右翼政党的、漂亮的白人蓝领郊区。

sentences.en: And what research onto this shows is that the people who get most upset and most freaked out by change are people who aren't experiencing it themselves but are kind of close enough to see it.
sentences.zh: 相关研究表明，那些对变化感到最不安、最惊慌的人，往往并不是亲历变化的人，而是离变化足够近、能看到变化的人。

sentences.en: So maybe they commute through it every day.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能每天通勤都会经过这些地方。

sentences.en: Or when they head into the city to go out to dinner or something like that, they see it and they don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 或者当他们进城吃晚餐之类的，他们看到了这些变化，却无法理解。

sentences.en: They don't interact with those kinds of people.
sentences.zh: 他们与那些人并没有互动。

sentences.en: And so it feels frightening to them.
sentences.zh: 所以这让他们感到恐惧。

sentences.en: So there's an upcoming election in the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 荷兰即将举行选举。

sentences.en: And I wonder what it tells us about the rise of the far-right in Europe.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这对于理解欧洲极右翼的崛起意味着什么。

sentences.en: The Netherlands election is a pretty interesting example of this.
sentences.zh: 荷兰选举就是一个非常有趣的例子。

sentences.en: All the polls show that Geert Wilders is likely to...
sentences.zh: 所有民调都显示，基尔特·威尔德斯很可能会……

sentences.en: His party is likely to either get the most votes or come second.
sentences.zh: 他的政党很可能会获得最多选票，或者位居第二。

sentences.en: And he is absolutely an example of this kind of far-right populist politics.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是这种极右翼民粹主义政治的典型代表。

sentences.en: But the question is, will far-right parties get enough voters to upset the existing political equilibrium?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，极右翼政党能否获得足够的选票来打破现有的政治平衡？

sentences.en: Are we voting, will this party, for freedom?
sentences.zh: 我们是在投票吗？这个政党是为了自由吗？

sentences.en: For our freedom.
sentences.zh: 为了我们的自由。

sentences.en: Our freedom, our rights, our Europe.
sentences.zh: 我们的自由，我们的权利，我们的欧洲。

sentences.en: Will there be enough voters, enough people to make a difference politically?
sentences.zh: 会有足够的选民，足够多的人在政治上带来改变吗？

sentences.en: And I'm fed up with the whole stupidity of importing Muslim scum into Europe.
sentences.zh: 我受够了把穆斯林渣滓引入欧洲这种愚蠢行径。

sentences.en: And that's the whole problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题的全部所在。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And I think what we're already seeing is something that hasn't gotten nearly as much attention as these really splashy candidates who say controversial things and get headlines.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们已经看到了一些现象，但它们并没有像那些言论出格、语不惊人死不休的候选人那样受到足够的关注。

sentences.en: A lot of people call him a raciSt.
sentences.zh: 很多人称他为种族主义者。

sentences.en: But he's not a raciSt.
sentences.zh: 但他不是种族主义者。

sentences.en: Because he said, if you are a foreigner, you can stay here, but just follow the rules.
sentences.zh: 因为他说过，如果你是外国人，你可以留在这里，但必须遵守规则。

sentences.en: But it may be even more important, which is that the populist platforms and policies are kind of starting to spread out to the other parties.
sentences.zh: 但可能更重要的是，民粹主义的纲领和政策正开始蔓延到其他政党。

sentences.en: And it's not that the populist candidates are persuading mainstream parties to be populiSt.
sentences.zh: 并不是民粹主义候选人说服了主流政党去搞民粹主义。

sentences.en: Mainstream parties are going to say, oh my God, we're losing our vote share to these people on the far right.
sentences.zh: 主流政党会说，天哪，我们正在失去极右翼选民的支持。

sentences.en: We need to change our platform a little bit to try to accommodate some of these ideas.
sentences.zh: 我们需要稍微改变一下我们的纲领，试图容纳其中一些观点。

sentences.en: A lot of politicians disagree with it, but they didn't really stand up against him.
sentences.zh: 很多政客不同意他的观点，但他们并没有真正站出来反对他。

sentences.en: And therefore, it has become more and more normal to say these things.
sentences.zh: 因此，说这些话变得越来越正常了。

sentences.en: More people are starting to believe it because it's not really challenged.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人开始相信这些话，因为它们没有受到真正的挑战。

sentences.en: This is something that for a long time people dismissed as just a protest or just a few disaffected people who could never be reached.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，人们一直认为这只是抗议，或者只是一小部分无法被触及的失意者。

sentences.en: But it's gaining influence.
sentences.zh: 但它正在获得影响力。

sentences.en: It's gaining popularity.
sentences.zh: 它正在获得人气。

sentences.en: As you've been traveling to all these European capitals, I wonder how often the name Donald
sentences.zh: 当你走访这些欧洲首都时，我想知道“唐纳德”这个名字出现的频率如何？

sentences.en: Trump comes up and the rise of Trumpism in the United States.
sentences.zh: 特朗普以及美国特朗普主义的崛起。

sentences.en: What do you hear from people?
sentences.zh: 你从人们那里听到了什么？

sentences.en: Honestly, I think I'm going to start taking bets on how long I can go before somebody asks me about Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我想我得开始打赌，看看我能坚持多久才会被人问到唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: It's not long.
sentences.zh: 时间不长。

sentences.en: It's minutes, not hours.
sentences.zh: 是以分钟计，而不是以小时计。

sentences.en: I think Trump, especially for people right now where Europe is grappling with this kind of far right populist politics as well, has become this like, it kind of reminds me actually
sentences.zh: 我认为特朗普，尤其是对于现在正处于欧洲极右翼民粹主义政治困境中的人们来说，已经变成了一种……这让我想起了

sentences.en: of the mirror in Harry Potter, where you can look in and you see the thing that you kind of most want to see.
sentences.zh: 《哈利·波特》里的厄里斯魔镜，你往里看，就能看到你最想看到的东西。

sentences.en: Gives us neither knowledge or truth.
sentences.zh: 它既不能提供知识，也不能提供真相。

sentences.en: So everyone looks in and everyone sees something else.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人往里看，看到的都是不同的东西。

sentences.en: I think everyone looks at Trump and they see either what they most want to see or what they most fear.
sentences.zh: 我认为每个人看着特朗普时，看到的要么是他们最想看到的，要么是他们最恐惧的。

sentences.en: Do the far right leaders that you two meet with, do they identify with Donald Trump?
sentences.zh: 你们两位见过的极右翼领导人，他们认同唐纳德·特朗普吗？

sentences.en: Yes, they do.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们认同。

sentences.en: But they're often careful not to say that explicitly because they know that that brings certain political liabilities with it.
sentences.zh: 但他们通常很谨慎，不会明确说出来，因为他们知道这会带来一定的政治负担。

sentences.en: Donald Trump is not popular in Europe, but they do understand that the message that he is carrying is very similar to theirs.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在欧洲并不受欢迎，但他们确实明白，他所传递的信息与他们非常相似。

sentences.en: And they like the idea of a fellow traveler running the West's most powerful country.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢由一个志同道合的人来执掌西方最强大的国家这一想法。

sentences.en: Max and Amanda, thank you very much for this intercontinental episode.
sentences.zh: 马克斯和阿曼达，非常感谢你们带来这期跨洲节目。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Voters in the Netherlands head to the polls on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 荷兰选民将于周三前往投票站投票。

sentences.en: Back in the United States, Iowa Congressman Steve King, an ally of President Trump, went on
sentences.zh: 回到美国，特朗普总统的盟友、爱荷华州众议员史蒂夫·金在周末发了

sentences.en: Twitter over the weekend to praise Gert Wilders.
sentences.zh: 推特，赞扬了基尔特·威尔德斯。

sentences.en: Wilders, the congressman wrote, quote, understands that culture and demographics are our destiny.
sentences.zh: 这位众议员写道，引用：“威尔德斯明白文化和人口结构就是我们的命运。”

sentences.en: We can't restore our civilization with somebody else's babies.
sentences.zh: “我们无法用别人的孩子来重建我们的文明。”

sentences.en: That tweet was widely denounced, but Congressman King is standing by it.
sentences.zh: 那条推文遭到了广泛谴责，但金众议员坚持自己的立场。

sentences.en: And I've said the same thing as far as 10 years ago to the German people and to any population
sentences.zh: 我早在10年前就对德国人民以及任何人口正在减少、

sentences.en: of people that is a declining population that doesn't isn't willing to have enough babies to reproduce themselves.
sentences.zh: 不愿意生育足够后代来繁衍自身的人群说过同样的话。

sentences.en: And I've said to them, you cannot rebuild your civilization with somebody else's babies.
sentences.zh: 我对他们说，你不能用别人的孩子来重建你的文明。

sentences.en: You've got to keep your birth rate up and that you need to teach your children your values.
sentences.zh: 你必须保持出生率，并且你需要向你的孩子传授你的价值观。

sentences.en: And in doing so, then you can grow your population and you can strengthen your culture.
sentences.zh: 只有这样，你才能增加人口，增强你的文化。

sentences.en: You can strengthen your way of life.
sentences.zh: 你可以增强你的生活方式。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: 24 million Americans would lose their health insurance over the next decade under the Republican
sentences.zh: 根据国会预算办公室这一无党派监督机构的一份备受期待的分析，在共和党

sentences.en: plan to replace the Affordable Care Act, according to a highly anticipated analysis from the Congressional
sentences.zh: 取代《平价医疗法案》的计划下，未来十年内将有2400万美国人失去医疗保险。

sentences.en: Budget Office, a nonpartisan watchdog.
sentences.zh: 其中1400万人将在第一年失去保险。

sentences.en: 14 million of those would lose their coverage in the first year.
sentences.zh: 制定该计划的共和党领导人，如众议院议长保罗·瑞安，表示他们预料到会有所下降。

sentences.en: Republican leaders who have crafted the plan, like House Speaker Paul Ryan, say they expect a drop-off.
sentences.zh: 当自由市场与政府强制令对决时，你永远无法赢得覆盖率选美比赛。

sentences.en: You're never going to win a coverage beauty contest when it's free market versus government mandates.
sentences.zh: 如果政府说，你们必须购买我们的医疗保险，政府的估算就会说人们会遵守，这就会发生。

sentences.en: If the government says, thou shall buy our health insurance, the government estimates are going to say people will comply and it will happen.
sentences.zh: 而当你用“我们将拥有一个自由市场，你想买什么就买什么”来取代它时，他们会说，不会有那么多人这样做。

sentences.en: And when you replace that with, we're going to have a free market and you buy what you want to buy, they're going to say not nearly as many people are going to do that.
sentences.zh: 白宫正在对特朗普总统关于巴拉克·奥巴马在2016年竞选期间窃听

sentences.en: And the White House is casting doubt on President Trump's weak-old claim that Barack Obama wiretapped
sentences.zh: 特朗普电话的陈旧说法表示怀疑。

sentences.en: Trump's phone during the 2016 campaign.
sentences.zh: 我认为他并不是真的认为奥巴马总统亲自去窃听了他的电话。

sentences.en: He doesn't really think that President Obama went up and tapped his phone personally, I think.
sentences.zh: 但我认为毫无疑问，奥巴马政府在2016年大选中确实采取了监视和其他行动。

sentences.en: But I think there's no question that the Obama administration, that there were actions about surveillance and other activities that occurred in the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 总统使用“窃听”这个词，加了引号，是指广义上的监视和其他活动。

sentences.en: The president used the word wiretap, in quotes, to mean broadly surveillance and other activities.
sentences.zh: 白宫已经错过了国会提供的任何此类窃听证据的最后期限。

sentences.en: The White House has missed a congressional deadline to provide any evidence of such a wiretap.

sentences.zh: 对我们东北部的听众，请注意安全。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
